language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello! My name is Imhotep. Every morning, I wake up early, together with my grandfather to watch the sunrise.
This morning I asked my grandfather where the sun goes at night. He told me that the sun isn't moving around the earth, it’s the earth that moves around the sun!
He said the earth is constantly spinning on its axis—that’s an imaginary line that runs through the earth’s center. So as the earth rotates, the sun looks like it’s moving across the sky.
But why can’t we see the sun at night then? I asked. Grandfather said that this is because our part of the earth is facing away from the sun. At night, the sun is on the other side of the planet.
I couldn’t believe that! All this time I thought the sun was moving around the earth!
Let’s help Imhotep learn more about the Sun!

My grandfather invited me to sail across the sea with him today. We left right after sunrise, and he said it will take all day for us to get to the other side. I decided to use the sun as a guide so that I would know which direction we needed to go.

When we started out this morning the sun was behind us, but now it’s the evening and the sun is in front of us. I keep trying to tell Grandfather that I think we’re going the wrong way, but he says we’re not. Can you help us settle our argument? Choose whether the following statements are true or false.

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: The earth has been moving all the time since we began our journey.

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: The earth has not moved since we began our journey.

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: Grandfather is right. If they want to get to the other side of the sea, they should continue sailing toward the sun.

outro.text:
Thanks for helping us settle this! The sun does not move around the earth, but the earth moves around the sun. That’s why you can see the sun in different places
during the day.
